subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram partial-stream finalization lacks clear delivery-mode observability (sent vs preview-finalized vs canceled)

question: Should this Telegram partial-stream fix proceed by rebasing and proving the linked PR, replacing it from current main, or folding only the remaining outcome semantics into the broader delivery contract?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the durable outcome boundary affects Telegram delivery state, hook/log observability, and the one-preview streaming invariant while an open conflicting PR already owns the candidate implementation.

options.title: Rebase and prove linked PR
options.body: Carry the delayed delivered-state invariant through current main, keep the Telegram fix narrow, and attach redacted real Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Replace from current main
options.body: Open a clean replacement only if maintainers decide the existing branch should be superseded, preserving the same regression coverage and proof path.

options.title: Fold into broader contract
options.body: Keep this issue as the Telegram proving case while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561 defines the cross-channel delivery outcome model.

recommendation.title: Rebase and prove linked PR
recommendation.body: Carry the delayed delivered-state invariant through current main, keep the Telegram fix narrow, and attach redacted real Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent path history and the cross-surface delivery-contract choice point make steipete the strongest available routing candidate.
